cap_MlInbox.text:
Capabilities: three-pane-mailbox, global-search, folders-and-labels, notifications-view, work-package-chips, bundled-notifications.
What you see: Level 0, browse. Olivia's inbox with twelve conversations in a full-width list next to the full folder column. Each row has one line: sender, subject and snippet, work package chip and date. The filter chips All, Unread, Linked and Not linked sit above the list.

cap_MlThread.text:
Capabilities: conversation-view, attachment-list, reply-and-forward, link-another, work-package-chip, expand-and-collapse.
What you see: Level 1, read. The folders folded to a 64 px rail with labels, the list at 410 px and the Lyon rollout conversation in a wide reading pane. The linked FEATURE #58412 is a clickable chip with its status in the subject bar, next to a quiet Link another; the X at the end of the subject bar closes the conversation.

cap_MlThreadExpanded.text:
Capabilities: expand-and-collapse, whole-message-view, quoted-text-toggle, attachment-list, reply-and-forward.
What you see: Level 1, read. The same Lyon conversation with all six messages open in full, each with a down chevron at the left of its header, and the subject bar button reading Collapse all. One reply shows its quoted text under Hide quoted text.

cap_MlLinkWorkPackage.text:
Capabilities: work-package-picker, number-search, search-scope-chips, link-form, link-scope, attachments-to-work-package, comment-in-activity.
What you see: Level 2, act. Both rails folded, Jana's Gantt conversation stays readable, and the link form sits in a 440 px panel on the right. The picker has 58231 typed under its label, the scope chips for project, open only, type and assigned to me, and BUG #58231 as the exact match, selected. Below it the whole conversation as scope and both options on.

cap_WpPickerStates.text:
Capabilities: work-package-picker, suggestions-by-reason, number-search, word-search-with-marks, deep-search-toggle, search-scope-chips, keyboard-hint, no-match-actions, openproject-unreachable, picked-row.
What you see: The same 440 px picker in its seven states, each with a caption saying when you see it: the empty field with three suggestion groups, a number typed, words typed with the matches marked and grouped per project, the deep search on with a line of matching text, nothing found with its two actions, OpenProject not reachable with Try again, and the chosen row with Change.

cap_MlSearchModel.text:
Capabilities: search-as-you, mark-on-the-item, list-of-links, linked-first-search.
What you see: Two lanes for a project manager. Left: finding a work package asks OpenProject as you, so you see what you may see there. Right: finding the mail or event of a work package reads the mark on the mail in the mailbox or on the event in the calendar, and one list of links in Nextcloud that knows who linked what. Three facts under the lanes.

cap_MlCreateWorkPackage.text:
Capabilities: work-package-from-mail, pre-filled-fields, quoted-description, link-on-create.
What you see: Level 2, act, both rails folded and the form in a 440 px panel. Sven Lindqvist's demo request, with the form New work package from this mail in the panel. Project, type, subject, quoted description, assignee and due date are filled in. Create and link makes the work package and the link in one step.

cap_MlCompose.text:
Capabilities: reply-in-panel, linked-reply, status-after-send, log-reply-in-activity, work-package-reference.
What you see: Level 2, act. The reply to Marc in a full-height 440 px panel on the right, the conversation readable beside it without its own reply buttons. After sending, the status stays in development and the reply is logged in the work package activity.

cap_MlNotifications.text:
Capabilities: bundled-notifications, comment-from-mail, change-status-with-comment, linked-mail.
What you see: Four bundles, one per work package. The bundle for BUG #58231 is open as a timeline with a comment box, Change status, Open in OpenProject and a line to Jana's conversation.

cap_MlWorkPackageEmails.text:
Capabilities: emails-tab, reply-from-work-package, link-an-email, unlink, mailbox-access.
What you see: OpenProject itself, with BUG #58231 open on the EMAILS tab. It lists Jana's conversation with Reply and Unlink, and a second one the viewer may not read, showing only sender and subject with Ask Priya Raman for access.

cap_MlSearch.text:
Capabilities: global-search, search-filters, work-package-filter, results-per-work-package, search-highlighting.
What you see: The search holds #58231 gantt with the filter panel open; the active filters live in that panel only. Results are grouped under BUG #58231 and other matches, with the matching words highlighted, and Jana's conversation is open beside its work package panel.

cap_MlStates.text:
Capabilities: empty-state, loading-skeleton, openproject-unreachable, openproject-sign-in.
What you see: Four miniatures: an empty inbox, skeleton rows while loading, a panel that says OpenProject is not reachable while the mail still works, and a panel that asks you to sign in to OpenProject.

cap_MlSettings.text:
Capabilities: user-settings-dialog, linked-openproject-account, link-suggestions, default-project-rules, link-defaults, notification-bundling.
What you see: The settings dialog over the inbox, on the OpenProject section. It shows the linked instance, two switches, the rules that pick a project per folder or sender, and what happens when you link a mail.

cap_MlMobile.text:
Capabilities: phone-layout, work-package-chips, bottom-app-bar, link-bottom-sheet.
What you see: Three phone frames: the inbox, the Lyon conversation with its work package chip, and the bottom sheet Link to work package with a suggestion and a green Link button.

cap_MlLinkLifecycle.text:
Capabilities: link-lifecycle, link-on-reply, link-on-forward, link-on-move, link-on-delete, mailbox-access.
What you see: Six cards that say what a link does when you link, get a reply, forward, move or archive, delete the mail, or look without access. Each card ends with what the work package shows in OpenProject.

cap_MlThreadPanel.text:
Capabilities: work-package-panel, status-change-in-place, work-package-from-mail, unlink.
What you see: Level 1, read. The navigation folded to its rail, the list, the reading pane and the work package panel for FEATURE #58412 open at 400 px on the right. Frame a: the status menu open under the panel's status button. Frame b: the comment composer opened in place by Comment.

cap_MlFolding.text:
Capabilities: fold-in-levels, three-things-rule, navigation-rail, conversation-rail, hover-to-peek.
What you see: The three levels browse, read and act as the real boards scaled down, with their pixel widths (245 · 410 · the rest; 64 · 410 · the rest · 400; 64 · 48 · the rest · 440), and the four rules: never more than three things side by side, how a rail opens and folds with the panel icon, how the X on a panel or on the subject bar returns you a level, and that the work package panel opens with a linked conversation and folds with its chip.

cap_MlSettingsAccount.text:
Capabilities: acct-settings-window, acct-edit-settings, acct-remove, acct-default-mode, acct-special-folders, fold-subscribed-only, fold-sync-choice, acct-mailto-handler.
What you see: The settings dialog over the dimmed inbox, open on Account, with the shared section list on the left. A mailbox chooser at the top, then the server and password block with a refused-password error and Remove account, the writing mode radios, the six special folder choosers, the switch that hides folders switched off on the server with a per-folder background sync table, and under For the whole app the mailto switch and the app version with Copy version.

cap_MlAdminDomains.text:
Capabilities: adm-domains, adm-search-domains, adm-domain-area, adm-console, adm-quota-default.
What you see: Three frames. The Domains page alone with its search, four domains with DNS state, mailboxes, storage used and storage per mailbox, and the default storage per mailbox that every domain and person inherits (start of the storage chain). The same list with one domain selected and a short summary panel with Open domain and Remove domain. The New domain dialog over the dimmed page.

cap_MlSetupAccount.text:
Capabilities: acct-setup-page, acct-add-auto, acct-add-manual, acct-connection-security, acct-connect-google, acct-connect-microsoft, acct-signin-other-address.
What you see: The first screen when there is no mailbox yet: a centred card with name, address and password, Sign in with Google and Sign in with Microsoft, and the manual part unfolded with both servers, their ports and the connection security per server. Beside it the notice that the workspace account has no mailbox, with a field to sign in with another address.

cap_MlNavStates.text:
Capabilities: acct-switch-mailbox, acct-warning-reconnect, fold-combined-inbox, fold-create-sub, fold-delete-all, fold-repair, fold-view-assigned, comp-outbox.
What you see: Three folder columns side by side: the mailbox switcher open with three accounts, their unread counts, drag handles and one account that cannot connect with a password field; the menu of the folder Customers open with every folder action; and the views Assigned to me, Unassigned, Mentioned and Starred above the folders with an outbox holding two messages, each with Send now and Delete.

cap_MlListStates.text:
Capabilities: list-badges, list-labels, list-delivery-state, list-assignee, list-row-actions, list-filter, list-sort-fields, fold-priority-inbox.
What you see: The conversation list in four states: rows under date headings with every mark a row can carry and the actions of one hovered row, the filter menu open, the sort menu open, and the priority inbox at the browse level split into important, favourites, follow up and other.

cap_MlListSelection.text:
Capabilities: list-select-multi, list-select-all, list-keys, list-bulk-archive-delete, list-bulk-move, list-bulk-forward, list-drag-move, list-bulk-drafts.
What you see: Level 0, browse, with checkboxes on and five conversations selected. The bulk bar has labelled Archive, Delete, Mark as read, Move to folder, Labels and Forward as attachments, a More menu and a Keyboard shortcuts link; the selection is dragged onto the folder Lyon. Below, the drafts folder with two drafts selected and Delete 2 drafts, then the More menu open (star, important, unread, spam, not spam) and the keyboard shortcuts open, each in its own frame.

cap_MlMessageMenu.text:
Capabilities: read-view-source, read-download-source, read-print, read-mark-read-upto, read-mark-unread-from, read-delete-single, fold-copy-message-link, comp-forward-attached.
What you see: Level 1, read. The conversation toolbar with labelled Delete and Archive, one tooltip and a Conversation menu; the Lyon conversation with the menu of Marc's latest message open, headed with the message it belongs to, from Forward as attachment to Delete this message. Below it, the original message in a dialog over the dimmed conversation with Download the original message file.

cap_MlMessageStates.text:
Capabilities: read-receipt-send, read-unsub-click, read-parse-notice, att-spam-block, read-restore, read-html-isolated, read-delivery-state, read-sender-card.
What you see: Fourteen lettered frames of the reading pane. Six notices above a message, six ways a message is shown (isolated HTML with inline images, plain text with links, a train booking card, the chat layout, labels above the subject, a shared mailbox sender), then the delivery table of a sent message with the server's line, Retry and Cancel retries, and the sender card with matching contacts.

cap_MlAttachmentViewer.text:
Capabilities: att-preview, att-step-through, att-jump-source, att-open-message, att-zip, att-save-one, att-save-all.
What you see: The built-in viewer over the dimmed mailbox with one PDF, the message it came from as a link, Download and Save to Files, and arrows to the next attachment of the conversation. Below it the attachment strip of Tom's message with Download all as zip, Save all to Files, the tooltip of one row icon, and the attached .eml opened read-only with Open as its own conversation; a third frame shows the folder chooser that Save all to Files opens.

cap_MlSettingsSignatures.text:
Capabilities: acct-sender-name, acct-alias-add, acct-alias-edit, acct-identity-order, acct-identity-reply-bcc, acct-sig-default, acct-sig-variables, acct-sig-forced.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Signatures and sender addresses. A sender address table with drag handles, the sender name, reply-to and blind copy under each address, Edit and Delete per row and Add sender address; a signature table with a default radio, an on or off switch per signature, a Used for chooser per account or alias and one signature locked by the domain administrator; and the editor with the Insert variable menu open.

cap_MlSettingsAutoReply.text:
Capabilities: acct-reply-setup, acct-reply-range, acct-reply-weekly, acct-reply-timezone, acct-reply-indicator, org-away-period, org-away-format, org-away-profile.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Automatic reply, the one place it is set. The switch, subject, a formatted and a plain text, the switch that follows the absence in the profile, the schedule with Between two dates chosen and the weekly option greyed out, the time zone, Save and a test reply, and the header reminder that the reply is on.

cap_MlSettingsAppearance.text:
Capabilities: list-layout, list-density, list-favourites-top, read-mark-read-rule, comp-reply-position, comp-send-default, comp-send-sound, inv-auto-tentative.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Appearance and behaviour: the three layouts as pictures, the message list switches, when a message counts as read; under Writing and sending the reply position, the default send button and the sent sound; and under Calendar the switch that adds invitations as tentative.

cap_MlRules.text:
Capabilities: org-filter-rules, org-filter-toggle, org-filter-rerun, org-forward-all.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Rules. A read-only status line that the automatic reply is on, with a link to its section, and the Forward all mail card with an address and Keep a copy. Below, the rule table with drag handles for priority and a switch per rule, the strip that runs the rules over a chosen folder with Run now, and New rule.

cap_MlOrganiseSettings.text:
Capabilities: search-body-priority, search-body-account, search-attachment-text, org-trash-autoempty, org-spam-block.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Search and clean-up: message bodies for the inbox sorted by importance, a per-mailbox table for searching bodies, attachments, the trash that empties itself after a number of days, and the blocked senders with Block sender or domain and a link to the trusted senders.

cap_MlComposeWindow.text:
Capabilities: comp-window-popup, comp-windows-several, comp-choose-sender, comp-cc-bcc, con-suggest-book, comp-send-later, att-drop, att-forward-with.
What you see: Eight frames. The docked compose window over the inbox with a second message minimised, the Attach menu open and a file list with Send as a link per row; the recipient suggestions open; the contact card open; a reply moved out of the right panel; a message started from a mailto link with the From menu open; a forward with the original attachments and the read confirmation in an options row; the send menu of the split Send button; and a designer note on the three ways to write.

cap_MlComposeEditor.text:
Capabilities: comp-format, comp-html-source, comp-find-replace, comp-rich-plain, comp-slash-menu, comp-emoji, con-mention, comp-text-block-insert.
What you see: The full screen composer with Leave full screen in its head, the whole formatting toolbar with the signature chosen from it and one control for rich text, plain text or HTML source. Below, the slash menu, the emoji picker, a mention, find and replace, the HTML source, a reply with its signature menu open, and the text block menu in its own frame.

cap_MlComposeChecks.text:
Capabilities: subject-and-attachment-warnings, no-reply-warning, accent-warning, bcc-hint, recipient-and-size-limits, invalid-and-unknown-address, draft-dialogs, sending-and-undo.
What you see: Thirteen lettered frames, each a small compose window. Dialogs over a dimmed window for no subject, a missing attachment, accented characters, keep or discard a draft and replacing an unfinished message. Inline notices for a no-reply address, the Bcc hint, too many recipients and attachments over the limit with Send turned off, an invalid address and one that does not exist here. Toasts for sending with progress and for Undo in the first seconds.

cap_MlSearchAdvanced.text:
Capabilities: search-typed-operators, search-operators-languages, search-all-accounts, search-to-me, search-combine, search-size, search-skip-folders, search-platform-narrow.
What you see: Three frames. The search box in focus with typed operators, one-click chips and the account choice; the filter form opened to its full length with the and, or and not switch; and the platform-wide search narrowed to mail by date and person.

cap_MlLabelsManage.text:
Capabilities: labels-create, labels-edit, labels-delete-all, labels-nest, labels-expand-tree, labels-starter-set, ai-label-desc.
What you see: The manage labels dialog over the dimmed inbox, the nested tree with expand and collapse all on the left, one label edited on the right with name, colour, parent and the words the assistant reads. A second frame shows the empty tree offering a ready-made starter set.

cap_MlLabelsApply.text:
Capabilities: labels-apply, labels-create-inline, labels-undo, labels-drag, labels-drag-archive, org-drag-folders, org-undo-toast.
What you see: The Lyon conversation with the Add a label menu open and a toast offering Undo; below it two selected conversations dragged over the folder column, with labels, Inbox, Archive, Spam and Trash lit as drop targets and a Shift hint for label and archive.

cap_MlOrganiseActions.text:
Capabilities: flags-important, org-move, org-copy, search-folder-names, org-snooze, org-snooze-early, org-split-conversation, org-delete-forever.
What you see: The More actions menu open on the Lyon conversation, the Move to and Snooze submenus as their own frames, the same menu for a conversation in Trash with Delete forever, and two list rows: one snoozed with Bring back now, one with a quick action under the pointer.

cap_MlRulesEdit.text:
Capabilities: org-filter-match, org-filter-all-any, org-filter-move, labels-by-rule, org-filter-forward, org-filter-refuse, org-filter-stop, org-filter-script-check.
What you see: Edit rule opens inside the settings dialog in place of the Rules list, with Back to rules; the Form tab shows three conditions and the actions, Forward or Redirect as a choice and the two mail-losing actions under Stop the mail; the Script tab shows only this rule's lines with the mistake underlined and named by line.

cap_MlRulesScripts.text:
Capabilities: org-filter-script-manage, org-filter-script-edit.
What you see: The Rules section of the settings dialog: the rules of the mailbox with their switches and Add rule, then Edit as script with your own scripts, one active at a time, Edit, Rename and Delete per row, a note on what switching does to the form rules, and Upload a script.

cap_MlSharedDelegation.text:
Capabilities: deleg-give, deleg-who, deleg-open, deleg-accounts, deleg-send-as.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Delegation for one mailbox. The people who have the Manager role on my mailbox, each with a May send as this mailbox switch, Withdraw and Grant the Manager role; the mailboxes where I have the Manager role with a Shown beside my own mailbox switch per row and Withdraw; and how mail from a managed mailbox is signed, with the From choice sent by Olivia Brandt.

cap_MlNotificationSettings.text:
Capabilities: notif-kinds, notif-list-devices, notif-rename-device, notif-signout-device.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Notifications: four check boxes for what to be notified about, then the devices that receive notifications with last seen, Rename and Sign out, and the rename form open under the iPhone row.

cap_MlImportExport.text:
Capabilities: imp-imap, imp-detect, imp-mbox, imp-pst, imp-eml, imp-large-upload, imp-progress, imp-cancel.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Import and export: the new import radios with the IMAP form open and the server detected from the address, a large archive uploading in parts with Abort, the list of imports with progress, failed count, scheduled checking with Pause and Resume, Cancel and delete and Remove from the list, the export of the whole mailbox at the foot, and the running-import indicator in the header behind the dialog.

cap_MlPrivacySettings.text:
Capabilities: sec-sender-pictures-off, sec-trusted-sender-list, sec-external-highlight, sec-no-learning, sec-cert-import, sec-cert-list, sec-cert-assign.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Privacy and security: sender pictures from outside services switched off with the senders whose pictures are always shown and Remove, the external marking switch with my own domains, the learning switch off, the certificates with issuer, expiry and Delete, Import certificate, and a certificate chooser per account and alias.

cap_MlNotificationStates.text:
Capabilities: notif-browser, notif-sent-confirm, notif-quota, notif-bounce, notif-delegation, notif-app-update, notif-mention-marker, flags-answered.
What you see: Seven lettered frames: a browser notification for new mail, the Message sent toast with Take back, the storage line turned into a nearly full warning, a could not be delivered notice on a sent message, the notices when an account is delegated to you and when that ends, the new version line with Reload, and list rows with the unread mention marker and the answered and forwarded marks.

cap_MlInvitationCard.text:
Capabilities: inv-see-card, inv-organiser, inv-recurrence, inv-clashes, inv-answer, inv-choose-calendar, inv-update-cancel, inv-import-file.
What you see: The invitation from Tom as an event card in the open message with Accept, Maybe and Decline, the calendar chooser, Open in Calendar and Download .ics; six smaller frames show the updated, tentative and cancelled states, an answer to your own invitation, an attached calendar file imported into a calendar, and a booking found in a message.

cap_MlEventFromMail.text:
Capabilities: inv-create-event, inv-create-task, inv-proposal, ai-event-draft.
What you see: Marc's message with its menu open on New event from this mail; the right panel holds the generated title and description with Clear title and description, the Event or Task choice, when, calendar, people taken from the mail, and Send as an invitation or Save only in my calendar.

cap_MlSharedAccess.text:
Capabilities: share-mailbox, share-roles, share-read-only, share-last-admin, search-address-prefix, folder-share, folder-share-group, folder-fine-rights.
What you see: Two dialogs over the dimmed inbox. Who can use the mailbox Support lists three members with a role each, a field that finds people of the same domain from three typed letters, the notice that the last admin cannot be removed, and Leave this mailbox. Who can use the folder Lyon gives read or write to people, a group and Everyone signed in, with the separate rights unfolded for Tom. The navigation behind them shows the shared mailbox Support and two folders of colleagues under Shared with you.

cap_MlSharedConversation.text:
Capabilities: share-conversation, share-conversation-who, share-leave-conversation, assign-people, assign-raise-role, assign-timeline, comment-write, comment-edit.
What you see: Level 2, act. Jana's Gantt conversation in the shared mailbox Support, with share and assignment lines in the timeline and two internal comments in their own colour, marked as never sent, one with a mention and your own with Edit, Delete and Copy link. The right panel lists who the conversation is shared with and their rights, Leave this conversation, the assigned people as chips and the offer to make a viewer an editor.

cap_MlAssistConversation.text:
Capabilities: ai-summary, ai-regenerate, ai-list-summary, ai-replies, ai-label-written, ai-translate-offer, ai-translate, ai-followup.
What you see: Level 1, read. Jana's German conversation with a generated summary under the subject bar, marked as such with Regenerate and Dismiss, a bar that says the message is in German with a language choice and Translate, three suggested replies above Reply with the switch that labels your reply as written with AI, and the same label on Jana's message. The list shows generated one-line summaries instead of previews and a sent message with No answer after 5 days and Dismiss.

cap_MlServerProcessingRules.text:
Capabilities: srv-processing-chain, srv-combine-conditions, srv-footer, srv-subject-prefix, srv-edit-headers, srv-redirect, srv-mailing-lists, srv-error-handling.
What you see: The administration page open on Processing rules: a test field that lists the rewrite rules that apply to one address, then seven rules in order, each reading when this, then that in plain words. The fourth rule is open in the right panel with its conditions joined by and, or and not, its actions, and the Add action menu drawn open.

cap_MlIntegrationWebhooks.text:
Capabilities: int-webhook-forward, int-webhook-trigger, int-webhook-payload, int-secure-webhook, int-post-headers, int-contact-form, int-api-key, int-pause-integration.
What you see: The integrations page with five integrations of three kinds, each with its state and a Pause or Resume action, and the OpenProject webhook open in the right panel: web address, when it fires, whole message or headers only, signature or static key, Regenerate secret. Below it two further panels as frames: the website form with its subject line and labels, and an API key shown once after creation.

cap_MlAdminSettings.text:
Capabilities: adm-allow-own-accounts, adm-feature-flags, acct-protocol-sso, adm-directory-users, adm-google-client, lang-force, int-caldav, adm-tpl-create.
What you see: Four frames. Settings, tab General, with defaults for new users, custom fields, language and look, product features and the save row. The page People and sign-in (its own navigation entry) with the sign-in card moved from Mail server, Google and Microsoft sign-in, admitted groups, where people come from and every administrator with their scope. Settings, tab Connected services. The page Account templates (its own navigation entry) with one template per domain and the open template, its filter server, the two master sign-in options each with a security line, the preview, and Create accounts now and Remove with accounts.

cap_MlAssistAdministration.text:
Capabilities: ai-model, adm-ai-switch.
What you see: The Assistant page of the administration with only the assistant: the OpenAI-compatible service with address, key, model name and Test connection, the switch for language model features for the whole server with what it is used for and what data leaves the server, and the save row. Language and look moved to Settings, access to people's mailboxes and restore to the mailbox page, export of deleted mail to Queues and recovery.

cap_MlAdminQueuesRecovery.text:
Capabilities: adm-queue-view, adm-queue-remove, adm-flush-delayed, adm-reprocess-stuck, adm-read-setaside, adm-failed-events, adm-restore-deleted, adm-recovery-retention.
What you see: Three lettered frames of one administration page: the Queues tab with the three queues, the 14 waiting messages filtered on stadtwerke-kassel.example, Remove matching mail and Send delayed mail now; the Set aside tab with the two failed messages and three failed internal events, Tom's too-large message open in the right panel with Retry sending, Reprocess and Delete; the Recovery tab with the 30 day retention at the top, Olivia's deleted mail filtered on sender and date, two messages chosen to restore and Remove for good per row.

cap_MlAdminHealth.text:
Capabilities: adm-health, adm-selftest, adm-connections, adm-mailbox-log, adm-tasks, adm-reindex, adm-repair-store, adm-train-spam.
What you see: Three tabs as frames. Status with the status table, the delivery self-test and who is connected right now (Cut off as a text button). Maintenance with the jobs table, what each job does on a second line under its name and wide scope fields, and the running tasks beside it (Cancel task, Remove from queue, Open report). Operations log with the mailbox operations log, its switch and retention, the latest lines and the save row.

cap_MlAdminProtection.text:
Capabilities: sec-greylist, sec-dnsbl, sec-arc-trust, sec-send-rate, srv-size-limit, sec-force-tls, srv-relay, sec-block-private-fetch.
What you see: The Protection page with four cards: Incoming mail (checks on the sending server), Message size (the one home of largest message, size of one upload, recipients, headers), Rates (connections at the same time, commands, sender, recipient, signed-in user) and Encryption and relay (encryption, relay server on two lines, server certificates), with the save row at the bottom.

cap_MlAdminMailServer.text:
Capabilities: att-pending-limit, adm-server-config, list-fast-view.
What you see: The Mail server page with three cards: Uploads (storage for uploads not yet sent, with links to the message size on Protection and the default storage on Domains), Server configuration (connection timeout, sync interval) and Performance (fast folder listings), and the save row at the bottom. Sign-in moved to People and sign-in, the upload size to Protection.

cap_MlAdminDomainDetail.text:
Capabilities: adm-dns-status, adm-dns-copy, adm-dns-auto, adm-domain-alias, adm-domain-admins, adm-domain-signatures, adm-force-signature, adm-quota-domain.
What you see: The page of northwind-consulting.test with the DNS tab open: each required record with its state, Copy all records and Create at DNS provider, and the danger block that deletes all data of the domain. The General tab (alias, catch-all, storage quota, administrators) and the Signatures tab (domain signatures, forced signature) are drawn as frames b and c.

cap_MlAdminMailboxes.text:
Capabilities: adm-create-mailbox, adm-shared-mailbox, adm-search-mailboxes, adm-temp-password, adm-reset-password, adm-mailbox-access, adm-group-address, adm-reserve-prefixes.
What you see: The mailboxes of northwind-projects.test with tabs Personal, Shared and Groups, search on name or address, the Close to storage limit filter, Message everyone, and the row menu open with Reset password and Manage access. Frames show the New mailbox form, the temporary password shown once, the access list of support@, the Groups tab with members and the reserved address prefixes.

cap_MlAdminMailboxDetail.text:
Capabilities: adm-extra-address, adm-sender-identities, adm-rename-person, adm-quota-person, adm-folders, adm-empty-folder, adm-set-filter, sec-require-2fa, deleg-admin, exp-restore.
What you see: The page of one person with six tabs drawn as frames: Addresses as one table (kind, sender name, may send), Limits with the storage chain and the save row, Folders with Empty and Delete folder as text buttons, Rules with the automatic reply as a status with a link and an administrator override plus the filter script, Sign-in, and Access and recovery with who may open the mailbox (Viewer, Editor, Manager, Grant and Withdraw) and restoring mail from an archive file.

cap_MlPhoneTouch.text:
Capabilities: mob-native, mob-signin, mob-install-web, mob-swipe, mob-pull, mob-longpress, mob-toolbar, mob-share-sheet.
What you see: Eight phone frames: the native app signing in through the system browser, the web client's install prompt, a lock screen notification that opens its conversation, a list with the pull to refresh mark and a row swiped open on Archive, Mark as read and Delete, long-press selection with a count bar, two compose windows stacked as cards, the formatting toolbar above the keyboard with a right-to-left line, and the share sheet for a downloaded attachment.

cap_MlLanguageAccess.text:
Capabilities: lang-use, lang-switch, look-dark, look-help, a11y-skip, a11y-shortcuts, a11y-list.
What you see: The inbox in Dutch with the dark colour scheme and a message open whose content follows the scheme, the language menu open in the header, the skip link on keyboard focus and a list row with the focus ring; below it the Help menu with Helpcentrum and Tutorials, and the Shortcuts section of the settings dialog with the keys for moving through the list.

cap_MlSecurityMessageWarnings.text:
Capabilities: sec-block-remote-images, sec-trusted-sender-pictures, sec-confirm-link, sec-link-mismatch, sec-phishing-warning, sec-spam-warning, sec-auth-failed-warning, sec-lookalike-name.
What you see: Nine lettered message cards with the warning strip between header and body: pictures blocked with Show pictures and Always show for the sender or domain, likely phishing in red with links switched off, likely spam, failed sender authentication, unverified sender, dated in the future, a contact name with another address, a reply address that differs, and the dialog that shows a link's real target with a warning when the link text names another address.

cap_MlSecurityEncryption.text:
Capabilities: sec-smime-encrypt, sec-smime-sign, sec-pgp-encrypt, sec-missing-keys-warning, sec-smime-verify, sec-smime-read, sec-pgp-read.
What you see: The reply panel with the protection menu open on Sign with S/MIME, Encrypt with S/MIME and Encrypt with PGP through the browser extension, and a notice above Send naming the recipient without a certificate. Beside it the conversation with the reading side: an S/MIME encrypted message with its lock line, signature results valid, invalid and unknown signer, and a PGP message opened through the extension.

cap_MlIntegrationPlatform.text:
Capabilities: int-dash-important, int-dash-unread, int-smart-picker, int-feedback.
What you see: Three lettered frames: the platform dashboard with the Unread mail and Important mail widgets whose rows open their conversation, the reply panel with the insert picker open on files, events, work packages and people with Insert link, and the feedback dialog with a text field and Send to the operator.

cap_MlSettingsTextBlocks.text:
Capabilities: comp-text-block-manage, share-templates, share-templates-use.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Text blocks, the one home of reusable text. My text blocks with name, text and shared with, the actions Edit, Share and Delete and New text block; the share form open for Demo follow-up with users, groups or a mailbox as chips; and the text blocks shared with me with Copy to my text blocks.

cap_MlSettingsQuickActions.text:
Capabilities: org-quick-define.
What you see: The settings dialog open on Quick actions, split off from Rules because a quick action is started by hand. The table lists each quick action with its steps as chips in order, a switch that puts it in the toolbar, Edit and Delete, drag handles for the order, and New quick action.
